sections.h2: Town or city: which Newburgh is yours
sections.html:
Orange County has two Newburghs. The city of Newburgh is a separate municipality on the river, independent of the town since it was rechartered in 1865. This page covers the town. If your deed or tax bill says Newburgh, confirm which municipality issued it before you look up dates and rules.

About 31,825 people live in the town, in 11,640 households averaging 2.71 people. Nearly four in five homes, 79.8 percent, are owner-occupied. Median home value is $375,700 and median gross rent is $2,159. Turnover is low, since 93.1 percent of residents lived in the same home a year earlier.

The town covers 43.36 square miles, hilly in the middle and bounded on the east by the Hudson River. Steep bluffs line most of the shoreline, so few houses have easy river access. Named areas include Balmville, Gardnertown, Orange Lake, Fostertown and Algonquin Park, which holds the town's only historic district, built around old gunpowder mills.

On hilly lots, a survey and a look at drainage are worth doing before you list. The housing stock spans farmhouses to 1980s developments, since the town stayed rural into the twentieth century and postwar years turned farmland into subdivisions. If your house is on a private road, find out who plows and repairs it before you list. Most roads are maintained by the town highway department, two are county roads, and the town also has many private roads.

Two interstates cross here: I-84 east to west and the New York State Thruway (I-87) north to south, joined by a direct ramp that opened in December 2009. Route 300 is the commercial strip, and Routes 9W, 17K, 32, 52 and 207 also pass through. Stewart International Airport sits partly in the town, though mostly in New Windsor. Commuters value that access, so put it in the listing.

sections.h2: School districts and who collects school tax
sections.html:
Property tax comes from the Receiver of Taxes, though school tax depends on your district. Four districts serve the town: Marlboro, Wallkill, Valley Central and the Newburgh Enlarged City School District. Who collects the school bill depends on the district:

  • Marlboro: the town Receiver collects it
  • Valley Central: the town Receiver collects it
  • Wallkill: the district's own tax collector
  • Newburgh Enlarged City School District: the district's own tax collector

Look at your last school bill to see who sent it, and give the buyer that contact.

Town of Newburgh assessment and billing calendar
DateAssessment or billing step
March 1Taxable status date and exemption filing deadline
May 1Tentative roll and assessment change notices
Fourth Tuesday in MayGrievance Day
July 1Final assessment roll filed
SeptemberMarlboro and Valley Central school tax due without penalty
OctoberSame school taxes carry a 2 percent penalty
JanuaryFull property tax bill due without penalty

The town has 13,027 taxable parcels. The Receiver does not allow partial payments or installments on property tax, so the January amount is the full bill and penalties start if you pay in February or March.

Four water and sewer bills arrive each year, and a 5 percent penalty applies after 30 days. Whatever stays unpaid is carried onto next year's property tax bill, so clear any water balance by closing.

Exemptions run through the Assessor: STAR, military service, senior citizen, disability and agricultural. Find out which ones your parcel carries. Its page links the state's Basic and Enhanced STAR credit registration and the forms for the other exemptions. The Code Compliance Department issues building permits and certificates of occupancy for new and existing structures and investigates code complaints.

Recording is done by the Orange County Clerk, who also receives the state transfer tax return, Form TP-584, within 15 days after delivery of the deed. That tax is $2 for each $500 of price and normally falls on the seller. Order a deed copy straight from the clerk for about $5, because third-party companies charge more.

Even with a cash buyer who takes the house as-is, the paperwork is the same. The sale is finished once the deed is on file with the clerk and water, sewer and tax balances are settled.

sections.h2: How a sale moves from offer to closing
sections.html:
After you accept an offer, the buyer's attorney requests a contract and a title search is ordered. The search looks for unpaid taxes, water and sewer balances and any lien on the property. A buyer who needs a mortgage adds an appraisal and an inspection, and the lender may ask for repairs or paperwork that stretches the schedule. A cash buyer skips those steps, so the closing depends mainly on title work and your own timing.

Plan for the property tax split. Because the Receiver does not accept installments, the January bill is a single payment, and your closing date decides how much of the year each side covers. Your attorney will work out the proration and put it on the closing statement. Keep the water and sewer receipts, since unpaid amounts roll onto the next tax bill.

sections.h2: Why timing matters on a Newburgh sale
sections.html: Newburgh's calendar rewards planning. If you list in the spring, the March 1 exemption deadline and the May 1 tentative roll are close behind, and a buyer who closes in summer will want to know what the July 1 final roll shows. A sale closing in the fall lands near the September school tax due date for Marlboro and Valley Central, with a penalty in October. A winter closing falls before the January bill is due in full. Whichever season you choose, ask the Receiver for the current status of every bill and put the split in writing.

sections.h2: Getting a Newburgh house ready to sell
sections.html:
Start the work a month before you want to close. Pull together your deed, a current tax bill, your last school bill, and the water and sewer statement. Ask Code Compliance whether any permit for past work is still open. Because most owners here stay for years, many houses have had additions or finished basements over time, and a buyer's lawyer will ask for the permit record. If repairs look expensive, compare a listing against a cash offer by what you keep after repair costs, carrying costs and taxes. A cash buyer can skip the appraisal and the lender's repair list, so closing can follow your own timeline.

Walk the property with a notebook and list every repair you know about, large or small, so each buyer hears the same story. Before closing, request payoff figures for property tax and for water and sewer, and ask your attorney to confirm who pays each balance and how it is divided by the closing date.

faqs.q: Is the population on this page for the town or the city of Newburgh?
faqs.a: It is for the town, estimated at 31,825 residents in 2025. The city of Newburgh is a separate municipality and is not included in that figure.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in the town of Newburgh?
faqs.a: The fourth Tuesday in May. The tentative roll comes out May 1, and the final roll is filed July 1.

faqs.q: Who collects school tax in the town of Newburgh?
faqs.a: It depends on the district. The town's Receiver collects for Marlboro and Valley Central, while Wallkill and the Newburgh Enlarged City School District use their own collectors.

faqs.q: Can I pay Newburgh property tax in installments?
faqs.a: No. Installments and partial payments are not allowed for property tax, so the January amount is the full bill, and penalties start if you pay in February or March.

faqs.q: Do unpaid water bills affect a Newburgh house sale?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid water and sewer bills are added to the next year's property tax bill, so settle them at or before closing.
